models.title: Wolf Sheep Predation
models.summary: A predator-prey system where wolves, sheep, grass, energy, and reproduction interact in feedback loops.
mechanics: Sheep gain energy by eating grass and may reproduce when energy is high.
Wolves gain energy by catching sheep and die when energy reaches zero.
Grass regrowth introduces a slower resource cycle that can stabilize or destabilize populations.

models.title: Segregation
models.summary: A Schelling-style neighborhood model showing how mild local preferences can create strong global separation.
mechanics: Agents inspect nearby neighbors and decide whether they are satisfied.
Unsatisfied agents move to empty locations.
Repeated local moves can amplify into visible global clustering.

models.title: Traffic Basic
models.summary: Cars follow simple acceleration and braking rules, revealing stop-and-go waves without any central controller.
mechanics: Cars accelerate when space opens ahead.
Cars brake when another car is too close.
Small slowdowns can propagate backward as traffic waves.

models.title: Ants
models.summary: Ants lay and follow pheromone trails, creating collective foraging paths from simple local behavior.
mechanics: Searching ants wander until they find food.
Returning ants lay pheromone that evaporates over time.
Other ants bias their movement toward stronger pheromone trails.

models.title: Market Dynamics
models.license: Curated v1 educational preview; see upstream model before redistribution
models.summary: Buyers and sellers adjust behavior from local price signals, showing how volatility and liquidity emerge.
mechanics: Buyers raise bids when they fail to buy and lower bids after easy purchases.
Sellers adjust asks from recent trades and inventory pressure.
The clearing price emerges from repeated local interactions.
